chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Hajjaj al-Khashab, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who was on a journey. So when he entered the city, he came with two witnesses, and when his wife met him at the door, he made them bear witness to his divorcing her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'A divorce does not occur by it.'

key_terms.الْمِصْر: The city/Province (often referring to the place of residence or a major city)

ai.seo_question: Does a divorce take effect if a husband returns from a journey and divorces his wife immediately in front of witnesses at the door?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a divorce pronounced immediately upon a husband's return from a journey, witnessed by two men, does not take effect. This ruling highlights the specific legal category of 'divorce of the absentee' (*talaq al-gha'ib*), where the timing and conditions of the husband's absence are crucial for the validity of the divorce, distinguishing it from standard divorce proceedings.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Hajjaj Al Khashab who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who was on a journey. So when he entered the city, he came over with two witnesses, and when he faced his wife at the door, made them bear witness upon him divorcing her. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘A divorce did not occur by it’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from al-Hajj aj al-Khashshab who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who is on a journey and when he enters the city he brings two witnesses, and when his wife comes to the door he asks them to bear witness to the divorce. He (the Imam) said, ’Divorce does not take place in this way.’”
